label: Claude Fable 5.2
output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Monday at Embakasi: casuals' pay, what to say and what to do (for Brian)

Brian, this is for you to read on Sunday. Everything in it comes from Kevin, Njeri, Peninah, Joseph or our own procedure. Where I don't have an answer, I've said so.

THE SHORT VERSION

- Money is on phones by 11am Monday, by M-Pesa. Kevin will not promise earlier, so we don't either.
- Each of the 212 casuals gets their full pay plus KES 500 for lunch and fare, with no M-Pesa charges deducted.
- You apologise in person, on behalf of management. This is our mess, not theirs.
- Talk to Ouma alone before you face the group.
- If his group still won't load, there are no threats and no talk of contracts. Call me if I haven't boarded.

WHAT HAPPENED ON FRIDAY

The bank upgraded its payment platform on Wednesday 25th and now requires a new file template. Our Friday file for the casuals was still in the old format, so the bank rejected the whole file at validation. Nothing was paid to any of the 212 people.

The rejection notice came in just before 2pm, but it went to an old finance mailbox. Kevin only saw it after 5, by which time the bank's cut-off had passed. Kevin has said plainly that this one is on finance.

You can tell the guys all of that. Nobody's pay was cut, withheld or questioned. The guys did nothing wrong, so please don't go in defensive. They are owed money and an apology, and Njeri has asked that the apology come from management, in person. That is you.

WHEN THE MONEY LANDS

Njeri approved the fix on Saturday morning. We skip the bank and send the whole lot by M-Pesa. Kevin's realistic time is money on phones by 11am Monday.

Say "by 11" and nothing sooner. Not "in the morning" and not "any time now". You remember Mombasa in 2024: the supervisor said "by lunch", the money came at 4pm and half the shift sat down. Joseph says the guys are already quoting the time management said "tomorrow" for three days. We cannot give them a time we can't keep.

Try to get a line from Kevin before you speak, to confirm 11 still holds. If anything changes, WhatsApp me. I'm up from 4:30 and my flight is at 7:05. If the time slips after you have spoken, tell them yourself straight away. Don't let them find out from their phones.

WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE

- Full pay for the fortnight, by M-Pesa, by 11am Monday.
- KES 500 on top for every casual on the affected list, for Monday's lunch and fare. It comes in the same payment.
- The company pays the M-Pesa charges. What is on the payslip is what lands, plus the 500.
- Peninah is at the depot from 7:30 with the list and her laptop. Anyone can check their name and amount with her, and she will print a payslip for anyone who wants one.
- For those with rent due on the 1st, the money lands the day before.

WHAT YOU MUST NOT PROMISE

- Any time earlier than 11.
- A time for the 14 people whose numbers Peninah couldn't reach (see below).
- Anything beyond what is in Njeri's email. If you think the situation needs more, ask her or me. Don't improvise in front of 200 people.
- That it will never happen again. I don't yet know what finance has changed, so say only what we are doing on Monday.

THE 14 UNREACHABLE NUMBERS

Peninah confirmed 198 numbers. She couldn't reach the other 14, mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake. If the number we hold is wrong, their money can't go to them at 11 with everyone else. They need to see Peninah face to face from 7:30 and give her a correct number.

Ask Joseph to help you find those 14 early and tell them quietly, before the general talk. That way they don't hear "by 11", then get nothing and think we lied.

I don't have a time from Kevin for how quickly those payments go once Peninah has the right number. If I get one before I fly, I'll add it here. Until then, give them no time. Tell them only that Peninah is there to sort it the same morning.

OUMA, AND IF HIS GROUP WON'T LOAD

Joseph says Ouma and two others are telling people not to load the Kisumu trucks until they see money. The trucks must leave by 9 and the money lands by 11. So you are asking them to load on your word, and their experience of management's word is not good. Start from there.

1. When you arrive at 5:30, get Joseph's read first: who is with Ouma and how many are wavering.

2. Talk to Ouma privately before you address the group. He is loud, but he is not a bad man. He has four kids and rent, and he is saying what many of them feel. Give him the facts above. Apologise to him directly and ask what he needs to see. You can't show him money before 9. You can show him his name and amount on Peninah's list from 7:30, and you can tell him about the 500 and the charges. Don't ask him to sell it to the others for you. Let him hear it first and decide.

3. Then speak to the group. Give the apology first and what happened second. Then say "by 11", the 500 and Peninah at 7:30. Keep it short and take the questions.

4. If the group still refuses, our procedure (v3, in this folder) is clear. A stoppage is handled by Ops and HR together, and nobody is dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day. That means no threats about contracts on Monday, from you, Joseph or anyone else, and no arguing it out in front of the whole yard.

5. For the HR half, call or WhatsApp me. If the refusal is clear at 6, call me then, not at 6:45. I'll be reachable until I board, and I'll switch my phone on the moment we land in Entebbe. While I'm in the air, treat this doc as HR's position. Peninah is there for numbers and payslips, not to negotiate.

6. You know how long those trucks take to load, so before Monday decide the latest time loading can start and still make 9. If you reach that time without agreement, stop negotiating and move to your fallback. You could load with whoever is willing, or speak to the mill about the slot. That is an Ops call and you know it better than I do. Missing the slot would be a bad morning. A threat made in anger would cost us much more than that.

7. Whatever happens with the trucks, the pay goes at 11 to everyone, including anyone who refused to load. It is their money for work already done. Please make sure nobody suggests otherwise.

AFTERWARDS

Anyone still aggrieved after the money lands goes through the normal route, Joseph first and then HR within 48 hours. I'm in Kampala until Wednesday evening, but I'm on the phone.

Send me a line once the money has landed, and tell me how it went with Ouma.

Achieng
